notes: The official DroidKaigi 2026 conference app (Play Store and App Store; the conference ran 1–3 September 2026). It is rebuilt from scratch every year by a large contributor group working to a design the conference's own designers produce, which is why a conference app earns a place beside the products here. :core:ui is the design-system module — KaigiChip, KaigiSegmentedButton, KaigiTextField, the timetable card, the profile card, and this year's hand-drawn Sketch and Doodle primitives. Counted in a checkout: 60 @Preview functions, all in core/ui/src/commonMain importing androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview. The first build proved the lane: with renderer: android the spec pre-flight passed and then :core:ui:composePreviewRender failed with "90 capture(s) were drawn and none produced a file. That is a renderer or classpath fault rather than a broken preview" — the Robolectric lane drew every capture and wrote none of them. So this renders on the DESKTOP lane instead, which is available because droidkaigi.primitive.kmp declares jvm() (jvmMain exists in this module) and every preview is in commonMain, with nothing Android-only to lose. It is also the lane closest to how this project runs itself: the repository ships app-desktop. previewAnnotations names LocalePreviews and LocaleScreenPreviews, the bilingual multipreviews declared over in :core:common: without them a source scan sees 34 of the 60 and fails every spec entry that names one of the other 26. Two other things a reviewer should know: several previews take their colour scheme through @PreviewParameter(KaigiSchemeProvider::class), and the repository is retired after the conference — the 2027 app is a NEW repository, so this import follows main until it goes quiet and is then either pinned or re-pointed. Apache-2.0. renderRuntimeProjects names :core:preview:impl. :core:preview:wrapper declares it compileOnly on androidMain and jvmMain — "impl stays off production classpaths", as its own comment puts it — and the binding is supplied at runtime by the app (devImplementation) and by the repository's screenshot-test convention plugin. A render of :core:ui is neither, so all 450 previews failed with ClassNotFoundException on DefaultPreviewImageResolver. Reproduced locally: with the project on the render's runtime classpath it goes from 0 of 450 to 450 PNGs. Run 81 rendered successfully — the first run on a plugin carrying compose-ai-tools#5044, whose empty-run gate had been failing this module's theme fan-out — and then failed in the catalog step instead: 'catalog component "language-toggle" produces duplicate output axes'. The cause is this import's own previewAnnotations. LocalePreviews and LocaleScreenPreviews fan every preview out into _en and _ja arms — 28 bases, identical sets — and the catalog's axes are variant, state, theme, size and props, with nowhere to record which locale a render is. Both arms therefore fold onto one key. Nothing here is misconfigured: the multipreview, the render and the error are all correct, and the model is simply missing the axis. excludePreviewIds drops the _ja arm so the import can publish at all. That is the wrong answer for a bilingual Japanese conference app — locale is precisely the axis a design catalog should show, because string length is what breaks layouts — so it is provisional and tracked in compose-ai-tools#5059; revert it once a locale axis exists. The _en arm is the one kept because this spec's captions are written in English.
